objective: Select the next validation goal after closing the Verilator-like operator-surface public-pack boundary.

decision.reason: The target-name plus --sim-accel-shape operator surface now has dry-run, execution, review, and public-pack evidence. The next useful gap is moving one step closer to the user goal: accepting a Verilator-like filelist-facing input and producing an explicit hybrid plan, while still avoiding hidden top/clock/reset/overlay/coverage-manifest inference and avoiding a universal automatic GPU-allocation claim.

candidate_review.name: filelist_to_verilator_like_hybrid_plan_boundary
candidate_review.reason: It directly addresses the desired operator model of passing design files and receiving a hybrid plan without making the larger native Verilator or arbitrary RTL support claim yet.

candidate_review.name: verilator_native_option_prototype_boundary
candidate_review.reason: Native Verilator integration should wait until the filelist-facing handoff contract is explicit and testable.

candidate_review.name: automatic_shape_policy_calibration
candidate_review.reason: Shape policy calibration needs a stable input contract first; otherwise optimization hides unresolved design-discovery assumptions.

candidate_review.name: larger_operator_surface_timing_repeat_median
candidate_review.reason: More timing evidence would not resolve the current usability gap.

candidate_review.name: resident_execution_optimization
candidate_review.reason: Runtime tuning should remain separate from defining the filelist-facing operator boundary.

required_next_gate.name: define_filelist_to_verilator_like_hybrid_plan_boundary_gate
must_pin: the minimal accepted filelist-facing input shape
which fields still must be explicit rather than inferred
how a filelist maps to an existing tracked target/template or refuses planning
how the plan reports top module, clock/reset, overlay, coverage manifest, shape recommendation, and compare report path
coverage_output_equivalence as the later correctness policy
generated reports and artifacts remain non-canonical
explicit non-claim that arbitrary RTL, optimal GPU allocation, or native Verilator support is implemented

non_claims: not a new runtime or ABI change
not approval to import untracked candidate overlays
not universal validation for arbitrary RTL
reports and artifacts are generated evidence, not source of truth
